question: Why does the TestShowFixtures class employ separate test methods for validating fixture documentation formatting across different contexts (trimmed docs, indented docs, first-line unindented, class-level fixtures) rather than consolidating these variations into parameterized tests?
answer: Each scenario requires its own inline fixture source file and its own full expected `pytest --fixtures` output (which must match docstring line breaks, indentation, and trimming exactly). Separate test methods keep each arrangement–act–assert cycle self-contained and readable; parametrizing would merely move large multi-line literal strings into parameter tuples without reducing real duplication, while making failures less immediately diagnosable. The tests were also added incrementally as documentation-formatting behaviors (e.g., docstring trimming, indented first lines, class-scope display) were introduced, so each new behavior naturally received a dedicated, independently named and isolated test.
